## Summary

Describe what this contribution teaches or changes.

## Learning objectives

What should a learner be able to understand, derive, build, use, experiment with, or evaluate after this contribution?

## Prerequisites

List the curriculum topics a learner should already understand.

## Contribution type

- [ ] New learning unit
- [ ] Expansion of an existing learning unit
- [ ] Curriculum / roadmap change
- [ ] Exercise or experiment
- [ ] Implementation improvement
- [ ] Documentation / contributor tooling
- [ ] Evaluation / reproducibility improvement

## Learning contract

Where relevant, confirm that the contribution addresses:

- [ ] LEARN — intuition and conceptual explanation
- [ ] DERIVE — mathematical reasoning where relevant
- [ ] BUILD — from-scratch implementation where educationally useful
- [ ] USE — standard library/framework implementation
- [ ] EXPERIMENT — meaningful experiments, ablations, edge cases, or visualizations
- [ ] REFLECT — failure modes, trade-offs, limitations, and when not to use the method

## Quality checklist

- [ ] I verified the code or notebook runs.
- [ ] I did not submit a copied tutorial or API-only demo as a complete unit.
- [ ] References and external material are attributed.
- [ ] The unit points to prerequisites instead of duplicating canonical explanations unnecessarily.
- [ ] I included exercises or completion criteria where appropriate.
- [ ] I documented important assumptions and limitations.
- [ ] I considered reproducibility and evaluation where relevant.

## Evidence

Add experiment results, screenshots, plots, test output, benchmark results, or other evidence when useful.
